newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ curve closes sharply steeper after wages data.
newsitem.headline: NZ curve closes sharply steeper after wages data.

text.p: * Dec bank bill futures 90.64 vs 90.69. Vol 1845
New Zealand's yield curve steepened considerably on Tuesday as the short-end sold off on bearish wages data and the long end rallied on hefty flows.
The 10 year bonds were yielding 8.17 percent at the close, off their lows of 8.14 percent, but still well down on the 8.28 percent close on Thursday.
Yields fell in the morning as one bank aggressively paid the market and even though they backed up, the market finished in reasonable tone.
It was a different story in the bank bill market where the December futures fell five points to 90.64 and the March contract fell seven to 91.26.
The market suffered from weakness in the currency and a reasonably weak T-bill tender, but the main influence came from May quarter wages data.
That showed total ordinary time wages rising 3.3 percent in the May year with private sector wage growth of 4.0 percent, ahead of most economists' forecasts.
"The latter will concern the RBNZ (Reserve Bank) which had been looking for evidence that wage growth peaked in the first half of 1996," said Bankers Trust NZ chief economist David Plank.
"Today's result is negative for bonds and positive for the currency," he said, adding that the next quarter's data on November 19 will be vital.
However, for the near-term, all eyes will be on the Federal Open Market Committee which is expected to hike U.S. rates by a quarter of a point when it meets in the later today.

Dealers are unsure what effect it will have on local rates, although the result is likely to be less pronounced here. Some dealers say a quarter point rise is already built in and the market could rally on such news. However, others suggest a smaller rise only means another similar hike in the near future.
"Any back-up from here will be reasonably limited as there are a few buyers around," said one dealer.
